sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: Gausul Azam Maizbhandari Polytechnic Institute operated across five separate buildings with no unified network infrastructure. Each building ran independently with ad-hoc connectivity, leading to IP conflicts, no centralized monitoring, and frequent downtime affecting 700+ devices including computers, IP phones, CCTV cameras, printers, and IoT equipment.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I conducted a full site survey across all five buildings, mapped every access point, and designed a scalable network architecture from scratch. The implementation was done floor-by-floor to minimize disruption to daily classes.

steps.title: Survey & Planning
steps.desc: Mapped all 5 buildings, identified 700+ device endpoints, designed VLAN scheme and IP allocation strategy.

steps.title: Cabling & Infrastructure
steps.desc: Installed Cat6A and OS2 fiber backbone, patched all endpoints, set up distribution racks in each building.

steps.title: Configuration & VLANs
steps.desc: Configured MikroTik routers, set up 5+ VLANs (Office, Lab, College, Schools, Hostel), enabled DHCP, NAT, and VPN.

steps.title: Monitoring & Launch
steps.desc: Deployed PRTG for real-time monitoring, configured alerts, tested failover, and went live building by building.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The campus now operates on a unified, scalable network with 99.8% uptime. IP conflicts are eliminated through proper VLAN segmentation and DHCP reservations. The IT team can monitor all 700+ devices from a single PRTG dashboard, reducing troubleshooting time by 40%. The infrastructure is ready for future expansion with fiber backbone capacity.

sections.title: Configuration Snippet
sections.configNote: MikroTik VLAN configuration for building segmentation:

config.code:
# Create VLAN interfaces
/interface vlan add name=vlan10-office vlan-id=10 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan20-lab vlan-id=20 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan30-college vlan-id=30 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan40-schools vlan-id=40 interface=ether1
/interface vlan add name=vlan50-hostel vlan-id=50 interface=ether1

# DHCP Networks
/ip dhcp-server network add address=10.10.10.0/24 gateway=10.10.10.1 dns-server=8.8.8.8
/ip dhcp-server network add address=10.10.20.0/24 gateway=10.10.20.1 dns-server=8.8.8.8

# Firewall Rules
/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-address=10.10.10.0/24 action=accept
/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-address=10.10.20.0/24 action=accept

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: The polytechnic's computer labs needed a complete overhaul. Outdated workstations, unreliable network connectivity, and frequent hardware failures were causing regular session delays for students. There was no standardized imaging, no preventive maintenance schedule, and the LAN infrastructure was unstable — affecting daily practical classes across all three labs.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I managed the end-to-end deployment from hardware assembly to network setup, ensuring every workstation was ready for daily use with zero downtime during practical sessions.

steps.title: Hardware Assembly & Imaging
steps.desc: Assembled 30+ PC workstations from components, installed OS images, configured drivers, and deployed to lab stations.

steps.title: LAN Infrastructure
steps.desc: Executed RJ-45 Cat6 cabling, patch panel crimping, switch configuration, and static/dynamic IP allocations across all workstations.

steps.title: Diagnostics & Testing
steps.desc: Performed stress testing, bench diagnostics, and validated each workstation before going live to ensure reliability.

steps.title: Preventive Maintenance
steps.desc: Established routine maintenance schedules, dust cleaning, driver updates, and performance monitoring for long-term lab health.

Each lab has its own subnet for organized network management, and the maintenance schedule ensures long-term reliability across all labs.

sections.configNote: DHCP configuration for lab workstation IP allocation:

# Lab DHCP Range Configuration
# Subnet: 192.168.10.0/24
# Gateway: 192.168.10.1

# Static reservations for printers
dhcp-host=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:01,192.168.10.201,printer-main
dhcp-host=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:02,192.168.10.202,printer-secondary

# Dynamic range for workstations
dhcp-range=192.168.10.50,192.168.10.199,255.255.255.0,12h

# DNS
dhcp-option=6,8.8.8.8,8.8.4.4

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.content: The campus had no centralized surveillance system. Computer labs, classrooms, and administrative areas were unmonitored, creating security vulnerabilities. There was no recording infrastructure, no motion detection, and no way to review incidents after the fact.

sections.title: My Approach
sections.content: I planned the camera placement strategy, managed the cabling infrastructure, and configured the entire surveillance system from hardware mounting to centralized monitoring.

steps.title: Site Survey & Planning
steps.desc: Surveyed all buildings, identified critical zones, planned camera angles and coverage areas for maximum visibility.

steps.title: Camera Installation
steps.desc: Mounted HD IP cameras across labs, classrooms, and admin areas with strategic positioning for full coverage.

steps.title: NVR & Storage Setup
steps.desc: Installed centralized NVR units, configured storage drives, set up motion-detection triggers and recording schedules.

steps.title: Cabling & Monitoring
steps.desc: Managed Ethernet cable routing, connector termination, and configured centralized monitoring screens for security staff.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The campus now has complete surveillance coverage across all critical areas. The system records 24/7 with motion-detection alerts, enabling rapid response to incidents. Centralized monitoring allows security staff to oversee the entire campus from a single station. The infrastructure supports future expansion with additional cameras and storage capacity.

config.code:
# Motion Detection Configuration
motion_detection:
  enabled: true
  sensitivity: medium
  zones:
    - name: "computer-lab"
      cameras: [cam-01, cam-02, cam-03]
      schedule: "24/7"
      alerts: [email, push]
    - name: "classroom"
      cameras: [cam-04, cam-05]
      schedule: "08:00-18:00"
      alerts: [push]
    - name: "admin-area"
      cameras: [cam-06]
      schedule: "24/7"
      alerts: [email, push]

# Recording Schedule
recording:
  mode: "continuous"
  retention_days: 30
  resolution: "1080p"
  fps: 25
